mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.0% consistently compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to lower cost of capital for firms and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.5 percentage points over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses corporate earnings growth and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and business investment, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through improved corporate revenue visibility.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS exceed 90th percentile, or interaction term coefficient < 0 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle economic expansions, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates sustained manufacturing strength, which correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economy avoids a near-term recession.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 in late-cycle regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.0% annualized growth rate consistently predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to anticipated monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL growth > 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A deceleration in monthly payroll growth below 0.2% over three months indicates weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in housing starts (HOUST) and quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days through heightened business confidence and consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where both HOUST and GDPC1 exceed 90th percentile, or interaction term coefficient < 0 in regression.

mechanism_narrative: During post-shock economic recoveries, a rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates accelerating manufacturing activity, which correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy regains momentum.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during post-shock recoveries when INDPRO rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 in post-shock regimes.
